provenance.method: Technology/accessibility expansion using current first-party Windows, Android and iPhone documentation without vendor efficacy claims.

question: Before installing another app, what built-in accessibility settings can I inspect on Windows, Android or iPhone?
why_it_matters: Useful accessibility features may already be present on a device, avoiding extra cost, accounts or setup burden.
current_understanding: Start with the device's own accessibility hub and the barrier you want to change: reading, input, voice control, motion, focus, display or sound. Feature names and availability depend on operating-system version, device and region. Vendor documentation explains what exists; it does not prove personal benefit or accessibility quality.
evidence_needed: Comparable cross-platform accessibility feature inventories maintained independently of vendors.
Usability evidence for cognitive and neurodivergent accessibility features.
reopening_conditions: A major operating-system release changes the relevant feature set.
dissent: Built-in features reduce setup for some users, while specialist third-party tools can be substantially better for particular needs.
